newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas stays mixed late, Aug still in range.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas stays mixed late, Aug still in range.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained mixed late Tuesday in moderate activity, with August still down slightly but holding the technical range amid little conviction about market direction.
At 1420 EDT, August, which expires later today, was down by 1.3 cents at $2.17 per million British thermal units, while September was three cents lower at $2.121. Other deferreds were narrowly mixed.
"It looks like we found a value range and we may just go out (August expire) here," said one Texas-based trader.
Most agreed a mixed fundamental picture had clouded opinions about about market direction.

While the bulls point to the potential for more heat, sluggish inventory builds and a hurricane-related supply interruption, the bears counter with forecasts for little extreme weather heading into August and ample storage. They note operators need to average just 67 bcf a week in injections to fill storage to 2.8 tcf by October 31.
"I think the potential is there for more upside surprises early in the month, but if they don't materialize, sentiment could quickly change in favor of the bears," another Texas trader said.

Chart traders agreed August was stuck in a range, with support still at $2.07 and the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance was still pegged at about $2.20. Further selling was likely at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.
Looking at September, support was seen at last week's low of $2.045. Resistance was seen first at $2.16, then along the down trendline in the high-teens and then at $2.20.
Technical traders said the sharp drop in open interest Monday meant the move up was driven more by short covering than new buying.
Cooler weather has arrived in the East and Midwest and is expected to continue through the week, with a slight warm up forecast for the weekend.
In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices firmed a few cents to near the $2.20 level. Midcon pipes were up slightly to the $2.10-11 area. New York city gate gas was little changed in the low-$2.40s.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's weekly AGA storage report range from 55 bcf to 90 bcf. For the same week last year, stocks rose 81 bcf.
NYMEX said 39,548 contracts traded at 1345 EDT.
On the KCBT, August was still unchanged at $2.11, while deferreds also were steady. The East/West spread narrowed by 1.3 cents to 6.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
